item.text: The Crime and Corruption Commission examined improper influence on Queensland state and local government decisions to identify corruption risks and possible safeguards.
item.support:
The CCC looked more broadly at examples and patterns of lobbying influence, decision-making and transparency across 
both state and local government.

item.text: It considered its information holdings and investigations, public complaints and submissions, and approaches used in other jurisdictions.
item.support:
was informed by our information holdings, analysis of the results of our corruption investigations, and the views and 
concerns

item.text: The CCC concluded that gaps remained in Queensland’s integrity framework, including risks from former officials’ connections, privileged access and undisclosed interactions.
item.support:
There remain gaps in Queensland’s integrity framework which allow for continued risk of corrupt practices (or the 
perception of them).

item.text: It proposed seven reforms covering broader disclosure rules, visibility of contacts, former officials’ lobbying, compliance audits, a shared reporting platform, board conflicts and education.
item.support: The CCC has proposed seven reforms for consideration by the Queensland Government
item.section: Appendix: Collated list of proposed reforms

item.quote:
There remain gaps in Queensland’s integrity framework which allow for continued risk of corrupt practices (or the 
perception of them).
Transparency of influence is currently limited by narrow definitions and reporting requirements.
